article_title: Vertically integrated medical education and the readiness for practice of graduates.
citation: Wijnen-Meijer M, ten Cate O, van der Schaaf M, Burgers C, Borleffs J, Harendza S. (2015). Vertically integrated medical education and the readiness for practice of graduates. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-015-0514-z
title: UHTRUST: Utrecht Hamburg Trainee Responsibility for Unfamiliar Situation Test
description: UHTRUST is an authentic performance assessment placing near-graduates "in the position of beginning residents on a very busy day", developed in Utrecht in collaboration with Hamburg and validated in a separate study following Kane's argument-based approach. It has three phases: seeing five standardized patients with unusual medical problems, a three-hour information-gathering phase with seven realistic distracting tasks and supervisor contact, and a reporting phase. Candidates are independently assessed by two physicians, a nurse and five standardized patients plus one SP simulating a relative, using facets of competence, EPA entrustment ratings, PPEFs and the CARE questionnaire.
requirements: All procedures identically designed in two languages (Dutch and German)
Frame-of-reference training for all assessors prior to the assessment
Pilot assessments to improve the procedure and rehearse the organization
constraints: Assessors were from the candidates' own country; no neutral assessors could be employed
Nurse scoring standards could not be compared between countries because of the low number of raters
examples: 59 candidates participated in July and August 2011: 23 from Utrecht, 7 from Groningen and 29 from Hamburg
